source: Cogitate Consortium (2025) Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness
finding: Largest adversarial test of GNWT vs IIT. Preregistered, peer-reviewed predictions on content areas, maintenance over time, and connectivity. Result challenged both theories.
numbers: N=256 total: fMRI 120, MEG 102, iEEG 34 (29 for decoding; 576 PFC and 583 posterior electrodes). Stimuli faces, objects, letters, false fonts; 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 s; 3 orientations.
quote: GNWT is challenged by the general lack of ignition at stimulus offset and limited representation of certain conscious dimensions in the prefrontal cortex.
limits: Only clearly visible stimuli, no visible vs invisible contrast. No-report design with task-irrelevant stimuli. GNWT proponents dispute which predictions were central.
agent_relevance: A workspace that only broadcasts on events is not enough, and evidence for a prefrontal hub holding all content is weaker than the textbook story.

source: Cogitate Consortium (2025) Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness (decoding prediction)
finding: Content could be decoded in visual, ventrotemporal and inferior frontal cortex. Category and face orientation were NOT decodable in PFC, against GNWT.
numbers: Orientation: iEEG BF01 5.11 to 8.65 for no decoding in PFC; fMRI BF01 3 to 71.5 in 34-55% of PFC voxels, evidence for an effect in only 1-9%. Category: adding PFC gave no gain, iEEG BF01 = 1.94e4 (faces vs objects) and 1.91e5 (letters vs false fonts); MEG BF01 3.05 to 4.70.
limits: Decoding in PFC is hard with mixed selectivity (Naccache 2025). Leakage from posterior regions possible.
agent_relevance: Do not assume the shared slot must hold every attribute of an item. Broadcast a compact selected summary and keep detail in specialist stores.

source: Cogitate Consortium (2025) Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness (maintenance and ignition)
finding: GNWT predicted brief PFC ignition at onset AND offset with silent storage between. Onset ignition appeared; offset ignition mostly did not. IIT predicted sustained posterior synchronization; it was not found.
numbers: GNWT window about 0.3-0.5 s per ignition. Posterior responses sustained for the stimulus duration (0.5/1.0/1.5 s). Content-specific frontal to early visual synchrony found (brief, alpha-beta in MEG).
limits: Offset ignition is not a central GNWT claim per Naccache et al 2025. Silent state is optional per them.
agent_relevance: Transient admit events with content held outside the workspace is a design choice not fully backed by data.

source: Cogitate Consortium (2025) Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness (connectivity prediction)
finding: IIT predicted sustained short-range posterior connectivity; GNWT predicted long-range links between high-level category areas and PFC. PFC showed content-selective synchrony; V1/V2 posterior synchrony was limited.
numbers: iEEG task-irrelevant trials: significant content-selective synchrony for object-selective electrodes in V1/V2 (4 patients, 21 electrodes) and for both categories in PFC (face-selective 19 patients). MEG: brief alpha-beta synchrony between face areas and PFC and V1/V2.
limits: Small electrode counts per category. Sparse coverage.
agent_relevance: Content-specific links between a central hub and early specialists is the supported part. That matches broadcast-and-read.

source: Naccache, Sergent, Dehaene, Wang, Farisco, Changeux (2025) GNW theoretical framework and the adversarial testing paper
finding: GNWT camp reply. Says the study confirms onset ignition in a 200-800 ms window regardless of duration and relevance, plus frontal to visual synchrony. Disputes offset ignition and PFC decoding as central.
numbers: Onset ignition window 200-800 ms. Stimuli lasted 500, 1000 or 1500 ms. No visible vs invisible contrast, so the central GNWT contrast was untested.
quote: it could not test the most central predictions of the GNWT, which tackle the critical contrast between conscious and non-conscious processing
limits: Authors are proponents, with a patent on consciousness monitoring methods. Not independent.
agent_relevance: Shows how defenders adjust predictions after the fact. Write test predictions before running our agent comparisons.

source: Naccache et al (2025), argument on decoding and PFC coding
finding: Decoding in visual cortex works even for non-conscious stimuli, so posterior decoding success alone cannot be taken as evidence for IIT. PFC neurons have mixed selectivity, which makes decoding hard.
numbers: Cites Dehaene 2001, Salti 2015, King 2016 for non-conscious decoding.
limits: Argument by proponents, not a new experiment.
agent_relevance: A module being able to read out a signal does not show the signal was selected. Check that the slot content is what drove the output.

source: Mashour, Roelfsema, Changeux, Dehaene (2020) Conscious Processing and the Global Neuronal Workspace Hypothesis
finding: Main current statement of GNW. Conscious access shows a non-linear ignition with late sustained frontoparietal activity. Report confound, P3b and PFC role are flagged as open.
numbers: Divergence conscious vs not at about 200-300 ms; N2/VAN peaks about 260 ms; dual task can delay access by more than 300 ms; retro-cue works up to 900 ms; infants: ignition-like at about 900 ms at 5 months vs about 300 ms in adults. Subliminal activity can last over 1 s.
limits: Read the first 100k of 274k characters only. Much evidence is correlational. Authors are proponents.
agent_relevance: Selection takes time and is delayed by load. Maps to the cost of queueing items for one slot.

source: Mashour et al (2020), working memory and attention section
finding: Attended working-memory items are proposed to be conscious and broadcast; activity-silent memories are not conscious until reinstated. Subliminal cues can attract attention without awareness.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Partial read.
agent_relevance: Memory outside the slot is inert until retrieved. Make retrieval an explicit step.

source: Sergent & Dehaene (2004) Is consciousness a gradual phenomenon? Evidence for an all-or-none bifurcation during the attentional blink
finding: Founding ignition result. Visibility ratings in the attentional blink were bimodal (seen or not seen) rather than graded.
numbers: Not opened this session; numbers not recorded.
limits: Later work finds graded awareness with finer scales or other tasks. The dispute is about the measure.
agent_relevance: All-or-none selection suggests a hard gate for entry, decided by code.

source: Del Cul, Baillet, Dehaene (2007) Brain dynamics underlying the nonlinear threshold for access to consciousness
finding: Masking study: nonlinear threshold in subjective visibility and a late P3 that follows it while early components scale linearly. Stillman 2024 reproduces the nonlinear awareness pattern in no-report form.
numbers: Not opened; qualitative only.
limits: Not opened; relied on later citations.
agent_relevance: Threshold gate with a large step.

source: Sergent, Corazzol, Labouret et al (2021) Bifurcation in brain dynamics reveals a signature of conscious processing independent of report
finding: Even with no task, EEG to near-threshold sounds bifurcates at about 250-300 ms: late sustained activity on some trials, none on others. It predicts reports.
numbers: N=20 analysed (25 recruited, 2 withdrew, 3 excluded). Single-trial prediction of reports AUC above 0.75 between 250 and 700 ms. Audibility ratings bimodal near threshold (modes near 0% and above 50%). Task-free access lacked frontal executive and premotor components.
limits: Auditory only, small N, model assumes bifurcation.
agent_relevance: Supports threshold admission. Also shows PFC executive parts belong to report, not to access.

source: Pitts, Metzler, Hillyard (2014) Isolating neural correlates of conscious perception from neural correlates of reporting one's perception
finding: With task-irrelevant stimuli the P3b disappears. A mid-latency negativity at 200-240 ms stays. So P3b tracks access for report more than perception.
numbers: P3b at about 380-480 ms only when stimulus task-relevant. Negativity at 200-240 ms in both conditions.
quote: some of the NCCs identified in previous studies may be more closely linked with accessing and maintaining perceptual information for reporting purposes
limits: Open question whether the 200-240 ms negativity is awareness or object-based attention.
agent_relevance: Keep 'selected for broadcast' separate from 'selected for output'.

source: Stillman, Drake and colleagues (2024) Neural signatures of visual awareness independent of postperceptual processing
finding: No-report visual masking with separate report and no-report sessions. Awareness was nonlinear in mask delay. A fronto-central N2 at 250-300 ms tracked awareness in both. P3b and temporal-generalization decoding appeared only with report.
numbers: Mask delays 17, 33, 50, 67, 83 ms: never seen at the two shortest, always seen at the two longest, 50% seen at the middle one.
limits: Full author list not recorded here. EEG, one paradigm.
agent_relevance: Replicates the report confound. Late ignition-like signals are partly task preparation.

source: Systematic review and meta-analysis of the visual awareness negativity and P3b (2026, registered report)
finding: P3b is not a necessary marker of consciousness (absent when task-irrelevant). VAN occurs even without consciousness, so it is not sufficient.
numbers: 117 studies, 547 seen effect sizes (322 VAN, 225 P3b), 89 unseen (55 VAN, 34 P3b). SMD VAN 0.37 [0.32, 0.43]; P3b 0.49 [0.41, 0.57]. P3b when task-irrelevant: SMD -0.12 [-0.47, 0.23]. Selective reporting may bias estimates upward.
limits: Only the abstract was read, via the Europe PMC record. Authors not captured.
agent_relevance: The late global signal is not conscious access alone. Do not treat a late-stage signal as proof that a thought is good.

source: Aru, Bachmann, Singer, Melloni (2012) Distilling the neural correlates of consciousness
finding: Contrastive analysis mixes the correlate with its prerequisites and consequences. Calls for designs that separate them.
numbers: Review; no pooled numbers.
limits: Abstract read through Europe PMC only.
agent_relevance: When comparing agents with and without a broadcast step, control for extra compute and prompt length.

source: Baars (1988) A Cognitive Theory of Consciousness
finding: Founding statement. Unconscious specialists compete for a limited-capacity workspace; the winner is broadcast to all.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Verbal theory; not opened. Neuronal form by Dehaene, Kerszberg, Changeux (1998).
agent_relevance: Design template: specialists, one slot, broadcast, code selects.

source: Goyal, Didolkar, Lamb et al (2022) Coordination among neural modules through a shared global workspace (ICLR)
finding: Replacing pairwise attention with a small shared workspace that specialists write to and read from helped on tasks where little input is relevant.
numbers: CATER object tracking Top-1 / Top-5: Transformer 70.83 / 87.8; hard-competition workspace 71.07 / 88.6; soft 71.33 / 88.3; ISAB 65.3 / 83.6. With RIMs on 36 Atari game pairs: median performance ratio 1.13 (game A) and 1.11 (game B).
limits: CATER gains are about 0.3-0.5 points, near the reported spread (baseline +/-0.44). Efficiency, not consciousness, claims. Mostly small synthetic tasks.
agent_relevance: A capacity limit can be a useful bias. Test narrow slot sizes in the scaffold.

source: Goyal et al (2022), Sort-of-CLEVR and Set-task results
finding: The shared-workspace transformer converged faster and to higher accuracy than a standard transformer on triangle detection and relational questions, and beat Set Transformer.
numbers: Shown as curves, no exact table values recorded here.
limits: Only plots; no exact numbers read.
agent_relevance: Fast convergence suggests the benefit may be learning efficiency; our scaffold does no training.

source: Devillers, Maytie, VanRullen (2024) Semi-supervised multimodal representation learning through a global workspace
finding: A shared workspace between frozen vision and text encoders, trained with cycle-consistency, needed far less paired data.
numbers: 4 to 7 times less matched data than full supervision. ImageNet linear probe from the COCO-trained workspace: 55.7% (+/-0.2) vs 50.3% for contrastive-only loss. Ablations: both the workspace and cycle training were needed.
limits: Two simple bimodal datasets plus COCO. Not a test of consciousness. Authors call for larger-scale tests.
agent_relevance: A shared latent between modules is cheap to align. Relevant for translating between code, text and memory views.

source: VanRullen & Kanai (2021) Deep learning and the Global Workspace Theory
finding: Proposes unsupervised neural translation between specialist latent spaces through a shared workspace with attention bottleneck and ignition-like gating. Position paper.
numbers: No empirical results.
limits: Conceptual; ignition and broadcast only sketched.
agent_relevance: Source of the idea: translate between modules rather than share one big context.

source: Dossa et al (2024) Design and evaluation of a global workspace agent embodied in a realistic multimodal environment
finding: A workspace agent built from Butlin-style indicators did better than a GRU baseline at small working-memory sizes in audiovisual navigation. The gap closed at larger sizes.
numbers: About 80% vs just over 60% (read from plots, no exact table); memory sizes 32 to 512; 5 seeds; behavioural cloning on 500,000 tuples; original SAVi RL agent 25% success.
limits: Single benchmark; authors say it is not a good test of memory capacity. Some size-256 runs poor. Author list not verified.
agent_relevance: Slot limits help most when memory is scarce. With long-context LLMs the benefit may be smaller.

source: Dossa et al (2024), probing and attention analysis
finding: Audio queries attended mostly to vision keys and the reverse. Probing found no clear link between representations and performance. GW agent did not keep target info after the sound stopped.
numbers: Probe chance: 4% for 21 target classes, 1.79% for 56 scenes. Target category from visual features 14-37%; scene from audio 6-14%.
limits: Read only the first 100k of 132k characters.
agent_relevance: Broadcast was used, yet the content did not persist. A slot needs a memory write, not only a broadcast.

source: Butlin, Long, Elmoznino et al (2023) Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness
finding: Derives four GWT indicators: GWT-1 parallel modules, GWT-2 limited-capacity workspace with selection, GWT-3 global broadcast, GWT-4 state-dependent attention. Transformers lack a binary ignition; Perceiver comes closer but falls short.
numbers: Four indicators applied to Transformer LLMs and Perceiver (IO). No scores.
quote: there is nothing akin to the binary ignition process in global workspace theory in self-attention
limits: Judgments are the authors' own and rest on computational functionalism. No test on LLM agents.
agent_relevance: The four indicators are a checklist for the scaffold: modules, one-item slot, broadcast to all, state-dependent selection.

source: Goldstein & Kirk-Giannini (2024) A case for AI consciousness: language agents and global workspace theory
finding: Argues that if GWT is true, language agents (LLM plus memory, planning, tools) may already come close to a workspace architecture. The claim is conditional.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Philosophical argument; no test. Disputable which agent part is the workspace.
agent_relevance: Naming our scaffold parts as modules, slot and broadcast shows structural match to the claim; it says nothing about performance.

source: Juliani, Arulkumaran, Sasai, Kanai (2022) On the link between conscious function and general intelligence in humans and machines (TMLR)
finding: Argues that access consciousness, a GWT-type workspace combined with mental time travel, supports generality, and proposes criteria for AI systems.
numbers: No benchmark results.
limits: Position paper. The link from workspace to generality is asserted, not tested.
agent_relevance: Pairs the workspace with simulation of imagined futures, as our plan-before-output stage does.

source: Doerig, Schurger, Herzog (2021) Hard criteria for empirical theories of consciousness
finding: Argues theories must make testable predictions with independent measures.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Our own claims about the scaffold need a falsifiable measure.
